title: RCB Fan Tribute Database (2008–2026)
coverLines: ROYAL CHALLENGERS BENGALURU - FAN TRIBUTE DATABASE
IPL 2008-2026  |  WPL 2023-2026  |  Built October 2026 as the source file for a static fan tribute website
WHAT'S INSIDE

Players - every player who played at least one match for RCB: 179 IPL men + 43 WPL women + 1 CLT20-only player (Nayan Doshi) in ONE sheet, each with a photo, RCB stats, and current status (still RCB / moved where / retired).
Key Moments - 45 defining moments from the 2008 debut to the back-to-back IPL titles and both WPL crowns - including 6 Champions League T20 moments (2009-2011) - with a photo on every row.
Grounds - all 31 grounds RCB have played at, with a photo for the big five, ground details, and the key moments linked to each ground.
Logos - all 4 crest eras (2008-15, 2016-19, 2020-23, 2024-now) with descriptions and logo images.

All Teams (IPL & WPL) - every team that has ever played the IPL (15) and WPL (5): city, seasons, status, home ground, owner, titles, captain & coach, full name-change history and logo-change history, with the current logo embedded.
Star Players - the all-time top 25 IPL icons and top 15 WPL stars, ranked, with why they're stars and their signature moment.
Seasons - every season's finish, captain and coach, IPL + WPL.   Captains - every RCB captain.   Records - the RCB record book.

Coaches - all 51 documented RCB coaches and support staff, 2008-2026: head coaches, Directors of Cricket, batting/bowling/fielding coaches, mentors, S&C, physio and analysts for IPL, WPL and the CLT20 years - each with a photo.

Franchise & More - ownership history and the 2026 sale, brand value, the 12th Man Army and 'Ee Sala Cup Namde', the Green Game, Unbox and the Hall of Fame, anthems, the Innovation Lab and ventures, and the story of the women's team.

4 June 2025 & RCB Cares - a memorial sheet: the stadium tragedy in which eleven fans died, who they were, the response and the accountability that followed, how they were honoured in 2026 (eleven empty seats, No. 11 jerseys, the dedicated trophy), and the RCB Cares commitments.
Squad Only - players who were in an RCB squad but never played a match (kept separate so the website never credits a match that didn't happen).
Website Guide - how to turn each sheet into website pages, image file-naming, and credits.   Sources - where every fact and photo came from.
HOW PHOTOS WORK IN THIS FILE

Photos were sourced from RCB social media and public sites, as requested. A photo is now EMBEDDED on every row of the Players (223), Key Moments (45), Grounds (31) and Star Players sheets - every image was visually checked, and wrong or broken results were re-fetched. For a handful of early-era players no RCB-kit photo exists in public sources, so a national/domestic-team photo of the player is used instead.

Every embedded photo keeps its original Photo URL + source credit in the row (Players sheet), so you can fetch the full-resolution version for the website. Photos display at a large thumbnail size - open the file in Excel, Google Sheets, LibreOffice or WPS (some quick-preview viewers do not render embedded images).

For players/moments/grounds without an embedded photo, the 'Photo Search' column gives the exact search phrase to use on RCB social media / IPL / WPL / public sites. Embedding all 220+ portraits would also make the file enormous - the website should load images as files, not from Excel.

Rights note: these are press/agency/franchise photos. For a non-commercial fan tribute, always keep the credit shown in this file next to each photo on your site, and replace any photo if the rights holder asks.
HOW STATS WORK IN THIS FILE

Player Mat/Runs/Wickets are RCB-only figures from one coherent compilation through IPL 2024 (ReadScoops full RCB list), updated where a 2025/2026 figure was verified (e.g. Patidar, Padikkal, Salt, Shepherd, the WPL core). Public sources disagree slightly (they count CLT20 and update on different dates) - cells are left blank rather than guessed. Before publishing the website, spot-check your headline numbers on ESPNcricinfo Statsguru / the official IPL and WPL sites.

Counts: 163 men played for RCB 2008-2024, +11 new in 2025, +4 confirmed new in 2026 = ~178; this sheet lists 179 rows (incl. Tim David's two stints counted once and Mayank Agarwal's 2025 return). WPL: 43 played. Squad-only names are NOT in the Players sheet.

websiteGuide.instruction: One card per player. Card = Photo + Player + Role + Seasons + Current Status badge. Detail view = full stats + Status Detail. Filters: League (IPL/WPL), Country, Role, Status (Still RCB / Retired / Moved), Star Player. Sort default: RCB Matches desc.
A vertical timeline page. Group by League, colour-code Category (TITLE rows in gold). Each moment links to its Grounds row and its Key Players' cards.
'Linked Key Moments' uses the exact Moment titles from the Key Moments sheet - match on that text to build the link both ways. Ground page = photo, capacity, story, linked moments.
An 'Identity' page: the 4 crests in a row with era + description. Use the two embedded logos now; fetch the 2016 and 2020 versions from the linked logo-history pages (1000logos / LogoLook).
Your homepage hero section: Top 5 IPL (Kohli, ABD, Gayle, Patidar + Mandhana for WPL) and a Hall of Fame page for the full 25 + 15.
A 'Journey' page: season-by-season table; Champions rows (IPL 2025, 2026; WPL 2024, 2026) highlighted. Captains as a horizontal timeline.
A stats/records page or homepage counters (973, 175*, 139, 263/5, 49, 2+2 titles).

Save website images as lowercase slugs: players/virat-kohli.jpg, moments/ipl-2025-title.jpg, grounds/m-chinnaswamy-stadium.jpg, logos/rcb-logo-2008.png. Keep the credit from this file in the image caption or a credits page.
Every photo row carries its source. Show 'Photo: <source>' on the site. This is a fan tribute - no official affiliation with RCB/IPL/WPL; add that disclaimer in your footer.
After each season: add new players to Players, new moments to Key Moments, update Seasons + Records, and move released players' Current Status. The 2027 auction will change many Status cells.

keyMoments.title: The Beginning - RCB's First-Ever Match
keyMoments.description: RCB played the first match of the IPL era vs KKR at the Chinnaswamy. Brendon McCullum's 158* won it for KKR - and showed the world what the IPL would become. Rahul Dravid captained RCB's first side.

keyMoments.title: Kumble's 5 for 5
keyMoments.description: Anil Kumble produced 5/5 vs Rajasthan Royals in Cape Town - still among the most economical five-wicket hauls in IPL history.

keyMoments.title: Manish Pandey - First Indian IPL Centurion
keyMoments.description: The 19-year-old's 114* vs Deccan Chargers in Centurion made him the first Indian ever to score an IPL century.

keyMoments.title: So Close in South Africa
keyMoments.description: Under Kumble, RCB reached their first final - losing to Deccan Chargers by just 6 runs in Johannesburg.

keyMoments.title: Kallis Masterclass Sinks Otago
keyMoments.description: In a do-or-die group game at the Chinnaswamy, Jacques Kallis carried RCB into the Super 8s almost single-handedly: RCB 188/2 (Kallis 73*, Uthappa 42, Taylor 32* off 11) beat Otago 108 all out by 80 runs; Kallis also took 3/18.
keyMoments.photoSearch: Jacques Kallis RCB Otago Champions League 2009 Bengaluru

keyMoments.title: Taylor Blitz & Bhuvneshwar's CLT20 Debut vs Delhi
keyMoments.description: Ross Taylor's 65 off 38 (Player of the Match) powered RCB past Delhi Daredevils - Delhi 138/6 (Kumble 3/20), RCB 139/2 in 15.1 overs. The match was also 18-year-old Bhuvneshwar Kumar's only CLT20 appearance for RCB - 16 years before he finally played an IPL match for the club in 2025.
keyMoments.photoSearch: Ross Taylor RCB Delhi Daredevils Champions League 2009

keyMoments.title: Kohli's 49* Books the Semi-Final
keyMoments.description: A virtual quarter-final at the Wanderers: Lions 159/6, RCB 160/4 in 19 overs - Virat Kohli's unbeaten 49 off 29 (Player of the Match) finished the chase after Manish Pandey (44) and Rahul Dravid (33) set it up.
keyMoments.photoSearch: Virat Kohli RCB Lions Champions League 2010 Johannesburg

keyMoments.title: The First Green Jersey Match
keyMoments.description: RCB wore green for the first time (vs Kochi Tuskers) to spread an environmental message - a tradition the franchise still keeps with one green-jersey home game.

keyMoments.title: Heartbreak in Chennai
keyMoments.description: Gayle powered a dream run after arriving mid-season (Orange Cap), but CSK defended home turf in the final - RCB lost by 58 runs.

keyMoments.title: Champions League Finalists
keyMoments.description: RCB reached the 2011 Champions League T20 final in Chennai, losing to Mumbai Indians - still their only CLT20 final.

keyMoments.title: Arun Karthik's Last-Ball Six
keyMoments.description: The greatest chase in CLT20 history at the time: South Australia 214/2 (Daniel Harris 108*) looked unchaseable, but Dilshan (74) and Kohli (70) kept RCB alive and, with 6 needed off the final ball, back-up keeper Arun Karthik - only playing because AB de Villiers had fractured a finger - swung Daniel Christian over mid-wicket: RCB 215/8, won by 2 wickets and into the semi-finals.
keyMoments.photoSearch: Arun Karthik last ball six RCB South Australia CLT20 2011

keyMoments.title: Gayle & Kohli Chase 204 in the Semi-Final
keyMoments.description: David Warner's 123* took New South Wales to 203/2, but Chris Gayle (92 off 41) and Virat Kohli (84* off 49, Player of the Match) added 141 for the second wicket as RCB won by 6 wickets with 9 balls to spare - a second consecutive 200+ chase, something never done before in T20 cricket.
keyMoments.photoSearch: Gayle Kohli RCB New South Wales semi-final CLT20 2011 Chinnaswamy

keyMoments.title: CLT20 Final Heartbreak in Chennai
keyMoments.description: RCB's bowlers did their job in the CLT20 final at Chepauk - Mumbai Indians 139 all out (Raju Bhatkal 3/21) - but the batting collapsed on a slow turner: RCB 108 all out in 19.2 overs, lost by 31 runs. Runners-up in both the IPL and CLT20 in 2011.
keyMoments.photoSearch: RCB Mumbai Indians CLT20 final 2011 Chennai Chepauk

keyMoments.title: Kohli-Gayle 204* Stand
keyMoments.description: In Delhi, Kohli and Gayle put on an unbroken 204 for the second wicket vs Delhi Daredevils - one of the biggest partnerships in RCB history.

keyMoments.title: GAYLE STORM - 175 Not Out
keyMoments.description: Chris Gayle smashed 175* off 66 balls vs Pune Warriors - 17 sixes, a 30-ball century, and RCB's 263/5. Still the highest individual score and one of the highest team totals in T20 history.

keyMoments.title: ABD's 133* at Wankhede
keyMoments.description: AB de Villiers' unbeaten 133 off 59 balls vs Mumbai Indians, in a huge stand with Kohli, announced the Kohli-ABD era at full power.

keyMoments.title: The 229 Partnership - Two Hundreds in One Innings
keyMoments.description: Kohli (109) and ABD (129*) added 229 vs Gujarat Lions - the highest partnership in IPL history. RCB made 248/3 and won by 144 runs, the biggest win by runs in IPL history.

keyMoments.title: ABD Rescues the Season - Qualifier 1
keyMoments.description: Chasing 159 vs Gujarat Lions, RCB collapsed to 29/5 before ABD's 79* off 47 dragged them into the final.

keyMoments.title: 973 Runs - and a Home Final Lost
keyMoments.description: Kohli finished 2016 with 973 runs and 4 centuries (both still season records) but SRH beat RCB by 8 runs in the Bengaluru final.

keyMoments.title: Badree's Hat-Trick
keyMoments.description: Samuel Badree took an IPL hat-trick vs Mumbai Indians at the Chinnaswamy - in a losing cause on a tough day.

keyMoments.title: 49 All Out
keyMoments.description: RCB were bowled out for 49 by KKR at Eden Gardens - still the lowest team total in IPL history. The low that makes the later titles sweeter.

keyMoments.title: Padikkal Announces Himself
keyMoments.description: Devdutt Padikkal scored 473 runs with 5 fifties in his debut season (UAE) and won Emerging Player of the Season.

keyMoments.title: Harshal's 32-Wicket Purple Cap
keyMoments.description: Harshal Patel took 32 wickets in 2021 - equalling the all-time IPL season record and winning the Purple Cap in RCB's playoff run.

keyMoments.title: Thank You ABD
keyMoments.description: AB de Villiers announced his retirement from all cricket - closing an 11-season, 157-match RCB career. His No. 17 became RCB folklore.

keyMoments.title: Kohli Steps Down as Captain
keyMoments.description: Kohli announced he would step down as RCB captain after IPL 2021 - closing a 143-match captaincy (2013-2021) while staying on as a player. The one-club story continued.

keyMoments.title: Patidar's Eliminator Hundred
keyMoments.description: Rajat Patidar's 112* off 54 vs LSG in the Eliminator - the first century by an uncapped player in IPL playoff history.

keyMoments.title: Kohli Passes Gayle - Most IPL Hundreds
keyMoments.description: Kohli's centuries in 2023 took him past Chris Gayle to the most hundreds in IPL history (he now has 9).

keyMoments.title: RR Bowled Out for 59
keyMoments.description: In Jaipur, RCB's bowlers shot Rajasthan Royals out for 59 - the third-lowest total in IPL history at the time.

keyMoments.title: Bangalore Becomes Bengaluru - New Crest
keyMoments.description: At RCB Unbox 2024 the franchise officially renamed itself Royal Challengers Bengaluru, unveiled the all-gold lion crest, and honoured the WPL champions on stage.

keyMoments.title: The Miracle Run - Yash Dayal's Final Over
keyMoments.description: After 1 win in 8 games, RCB won 6 straight. In the winner-takes-playoffs clash vs CSK, Yash Dayal defended the total in the last over against Dhoni to seal qualification.

keyMoments.title: RCB Hall of Fame Begins
keyMoments.description: Gayle and AB de Villiers were the inaugural RCB Hall of Fame inductees in 2023; R Vinay Kumar joined them at RCB Unbox in March 2024.
keyMoments.photoSearch: RCB Hall of Fame Gayle ABD Vinay Kumar

keyMoments.title: Shepherd's 14-Ball Fifty
keyMoments.description: Romario Shepherd blasted 53* off 14 balls vs CSK at the Chinnaswamy - one of the fastest fifties in IPL history.

keyMoments.title: Jitesh's 85* - The Record Chase
keyMoments.description: Stand-in captain Jitesh Sharma's 85* off 33 powered RCB's chase of 228 vs LSG - their highest successful IPL chase, sealing a top-two finish.

keyMoments.title: EE SALA CUP NAMDE - First IPL Title
keyMoments.description: After 18 years and 3 lost finals, RCB beat Punjab Kings by 6 runs in Ahmedabad (190/9 vs 184/7). Krunal Pandya (2/17) was Player of the Match; Kohli top-scored with 43 and lifted the trophy he had chased since 2008.

keyMoments.title: Qualifier 1 Demolition - PBKS 101 All Out
keyMoments.description: In Mullanpur, RCB bowled Punjab Kings out for 101 (Hazlewood 3/21; Suyash Sharma 3 wickets) and chased it in 10 overs - Salt 56* - to reach their first IPL final in 9 years.

keyMoments.title: Kohli Crosses 9,000 IPL Runs
keyMoments.description: Kohli became the first player in history to 9,000 IPL runs - every single one of them for RCB.

keyMoments.title: Back-to-Back Champions
keyMoments.description: Kohli's unbeaten 75 earned Player of the Match as RCB chased GT's 155 in 18 overs (161/5) in Ahmedabad - back-to-back titles, a feat only CSK and MI had managed before. RCB also topped the league table for the first time ever.

keyMoments.title: Mandhana - The First WPL Superstar Buy
keyMoments.description: Smriti Mandhana became the most expensive player at the first-ever WPL auction (Rs 3.4 crore) and RCB's first captain.

keyMoments.title: Devine's 99 off 36
keyMoments.description: Sophie Devine smashed 99 off 36 balls vs Gujarat Giants - the highest WPL score of the inaugural season, in a record chase.

keyMoments.title: Perry's 6 for 15
keyMoments.description: Ellyse Perry took 6/15 vs Mumbai Indians - the best bowling figures in WPL history at the time - then finished the chase with 40*.

keyMoments.title: The Eliminator Heist - Defending 135
keyMoments.description: RCB defended 135/6 vs mighty Mumbai Indians, winning by 5 runs to reach the final - Asha Sobhana held her nerve in the final over.

keyMoments.title: First Trophy in Franchise History
keyMoments.description: RCB Women ended the franchise's 16-year trophy wait: DC bowled out for 113 (Shreyanka 4/12, Molineux's 3 wickets in one over), RCB chased it with 3 balls to spare. Perry won the Orange Cap, Shreyanka the Purple Cap.

keyMoments.title: The 202 Chase - Richa's Opener Heroics
keyMoments.description: On opening night, RCB chased 202 vs Gujarat Giants - the highest successful chase in WPL history at the time - with Richa Ghosh's 64 off 27 the star turn.

keyMoments.title: The Record Final - 204 Chased, Second WPL Crown
keyMoments.description: In Vadodara, DC posted 203/4 - the highest total in a WPL final. Mandhana (87 off 41, playing through fever, per coach Malolan Rangarajan) and Georgia Voll (79) added a WPL-record 165; Radha Yadav hit the winning boundaries with 2 balls spare. Mandhana took the Orange Cap (377 runs) and Player of the Match.

keyMoments.title: Holding Both Crowns
keyMoments.description: With the WPL 2026 title following IPL 2025, RCB became the first franchise to hold the IPL and WPL trophies at the same time - and IPL 2026 made it a double-double.

allTeams.nameHistory: Royal Challengers Bangalore (2008–2023) → Royal Challengers Bengaluru (2024–present)
allTeams.logoHistory: 2008–2015: Original roundel — red and gold circular crest with an 'RC' monogram and a small silver shield bearing a gold lion. 2016–2019: Modernised roundel — the golden lion enlarged and made dominant, black added to the palette, shield removed. 2020–2023: Vertical black banner design with a large, simplified gold lion. 2024–present: All-gold lion above a bold sans-serif 'RCB' monogram, launched with the Bangalore → Bengaluru rename.

allTeams.owner: KPH Dream Cricket Pvt Ltd (Mohit Burman, Ness Wadia, Preity Zinta, Karan Paul)
allTeams.bestFinish: Runners-up: 2014, 2025 — still awaiting a first title
allTeams.logoHistory: 2008–2011 (as Kings XI Punjab): Silver and red shield with two lion heads facing outwards on either side and a top banner carrying the letters KJHPH (Kashmir, Jammu, Himachal, Punjab, Haryana — the franchise's catchment states). 2012–2020: Same two-lion composition refined — metallic silver crest with gradients and a brighter red. 2021–present (as Punjab Kings): New crest — a single large roaring lion's head drawn in gold gradient lines on a solid red shield, with 'Punjab Kings' lettering above; blue was dropped from the identity.
allTeams.notes: One of two original 2008 franchises (with Delhi) still chasing a first title; lost the 2014 final to KKR in the Glenn Maxwell season and the 2025 final to RCB after topping the league under Shreyas Iyer and Ricky Ponting.

allTeams.homeGround: BRSABV Ekana Cricket Stadium, Lucknow
allTeams.owner: RPSG Group (Sanjiv Goenka)
allTeams.logoHistory: 2022–2025: Winged emblem — stylised wings around a red cricket ball with blue lettering, in a blue/orange scheme drawing on the Indian tricolour. 2026–present: Full rebrand unveiled on 24 February 2026 — a coat-of-arms-style red shield with a frontal elephant's head at its centre, a crown above it and golden Garuda wings on either side; colours shifted from cyan/blue to red and orange. The three symbols are Garuda (courage), the Crown (responsibility) and the Elephant (strength and loyalty).
allTeams.notes: Bought for a then-record ₹7,090 crore at the 2021 expansion auction. Reached the playoffs in both of their first two seasons under KL Rahul; Rishabh Pant became the most expensive player in IPL history (₹27 crore) when LSG signed him for 2025.

allTeams.homeGround: Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad
allTeams.owner: Torrent Group (67%, since 2025) and CVC Capital Partners (33%; original owner from 2021)
allTeams.logoHistory: 2022–present (single era): A triangular 'kite / pyramid' apex emblem in gold, white and dark blue containing a lightning bolt — the shape is inspired by the kites of Gujarat's Uttarayan festival and the bolt symbolises energy and turning adversity into triumph. GT were the first Indian sports team to unveil their logo in the metaverse (February 2022).
allTeams.notes: Won the IPL in their debut season (2022) under Hardik Pandya — only the second team after RR 2008 to win with a new franchise core — and reached the final again in 2023 and 2026. Shubman Gill (838 runs in 2023) and Rashid Khan have been their cornerstones.

allTeams.status: Defunct (franchise terminated by the BCCI in September 2012)
allTeams.homeGround: Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium, Hyderabad (occasional home fixtures elsewhere in India) (unverified)
allTeams.owner: Deccan Chronicle Holdings Ltd
allTeams.captain: Kumar Sangakkara (final season, 2012); title-winning captain Adam Gilchrist (2009–2010)
allTeams.logoHistory: 2008: Red-and-black crest featuring a black-and-white charging bull with fierce red eyes, 'DC' monogram medallion at the bottom and gold/red lettering; jerseys were beige and black. 2009–2012: Modernised, sleeker crest in grey, blue and red — the bull redrawn with white eyes and modern sans-serif lettering; jersey colours changed to silver and blue from 2009.
allTeams.notes: Finished last in 2008, then won IPL 2009 in South Africa under Adam Gilchrist — one of the great one-season turnarounds. The franchise was terminated in September 2012 after owner Deccan Chronicle Holdings defaulted on payments/bank guarantees; Hyderabad's slot was re-awarded and became Sunrisers Hyderabad.

allTeams.homeGround: Maharashtra Cricket Association Stadium, Gahunje, Pune (2012–2013); DY Patil Stadium, Navi Mumbai (2011)
allTeams.owner: Sahara India Pariwar (Sahara Adventure Sports)
allTeams.captain: Angelo Mathews (final season, 2013; Aaron Finch stood in during that season)
allTeams.nameHistory: Pune Warriors India (2011–2013) — only name used
allTeams.logoHistory: 2011–2013 (single era): A spear-wielding warrior riding a galloping horse, trailing the Indian tricolour, set in blue tones (unverified).
allTeams.notes: Expansion team bought for US$370m in 2010; never reached the playoffs despite marquee names (Yuvraj Singh, Sourav Ganguly captained in 2012). Sahara pulled the franchise out in 2013 amid a dispute with the BCCI over franchise fees/bank guarantees.

allTeams.homeGround: Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, Kochi
allTeams.owner: Kochi Cricket Pvt Ltd (Rendezvous Sports World-led consortium)
allTeams.nameHistory: Kochi Tuskers Kerala (2011) — the name and identity were chosen by an online fan vote
allTeams.logoHistory: 2011 (single era): Stylised elephant motif in orange shades built around the animal's sharp tusks — the elephant, Kerala's state animal, was chosen to project domination and intimidation.
allTeams.notes: Played a single season (2011) after being bought for US$333.2m; the franchise was terminated in September 2011 for failing to furnish the mandatory annual bank guarantee. In 2025 the Bombay High Court upheld an arbitration award of over ₹538 crore to the owners against the BCCI for wrongful termination.

allTeams.status: Defunct (two-year replacement franchise; disbanded when CSK and RR returned in 2018)
allTeams.homeGround: Maharashtra Cricket Association Stadium, Gahunje, Pune (some 2016 home games at ACA-VDCA Stadium, Visakhapatnam during the Maharashtra drought)
allTeams.owner: RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group (RPSG)
allTeams.nameHistory: Rising Pune Supergiants (2016) → Rising Pune Supergiant (2017)
allTeams.logoHistory: 2016–2017 (single era): A purple/violet cricket ball flanked by golden wings, adapted from the RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group corporate logo; the crest was unchanged when the team name went singular in 2017.
allTeams.notes: Created for two seasons while CSK and RR were suspended. MS Dhoni captained in 2016; Steve Smith replaced him for 2017 and took RPS to the final, which they lost to Mumbai Indians by one run — the closest IPL final ever at the time.

allTeams.status: Defunct (two-year replacement franchise; disbanded when CSK and RR returned in 2018)
allTeams.homeGround: Saurashtra Cricket Association Stadium, Rajkot (also Green Park, Kanpur)
allTeams.owner: Intex Technologies (Keshav Bansal)
allTeams.bestFinish: Best finish: 3rd (2016 — topped the league stage, lost Qualifier 2)
allTeams.logoHistory: 2016–2017 (single era): Side profile of a roaring lion's head in orange and gold — a nod to the Asiatic lions of Gujarat's Gir forest.
allTeams.notes: Two-year replacement team for the suspended CSK/RR, led by Suresh Raina. Topped the 2016 league table with nine wins in their debut season before losing both playoff games; faded to seventh in 2017.

allTeams.homeGround: Mumbai venues — DY Patil Stadium, Navi Mumbai and Brabourne Stadium (WPL uses rotating venues; Mumbai is the team's base city)
allTeams.owner: Indiawin Sports Pvt Ltd (Reliance Industries)
allTeams.logoHistory: 2023–present: Uses the same Sudarshan Chakra crest as the IPL Mumbai Indians (2010-refined chakra design); no separate WPL logo era.
allTeams.notes: Won the inaugural WPL in 2023 and a second title in 2025, both times beating Delhi Capitals in the final under captain Harmanpreet Kaur and coach Charlotte Edwards; Lisa Keightley succeeded Edwards as head coach for 2026.

allTeams.homeGround: M. Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bengaluru (hosted RCB's home legs in 2024–2025; WPL uses rotating venues)
allTeams.owner: United Spirits Ltd (Diageo) — sale to an Aditya Birla Group-led consortium agreed March 2026, pending approval as of Oct 2026
allTeams.nameHistory: Royal Challengers Bangalore (2023) → Royal Challengers Bengaluru (2024–present)
allTeams.logoHistory: Follows the RCB franchise crests: in 2023 the team used the 2020–2023 black-banner gold-lion crest; from 2024 it uses the all-gold lion and bold 'RCB' monogram crest introduced with the Bengaluru rename. No separate WPL-specific crest.
allTeams.notes: WPL 2024 gave the RCB franchise the first trophy in its history; the 2026 title — won chasing a WPL-record 204 in the Vadodara final — means RCB hold the IPL and WPL crowns simultaneously. Smriti Mandhana has captained every season and was Player of the Match in the 2026 final (87 off 41).

allTeams.homeGround: Arun Jaitley Stadium, New Delhi (hosted DC's home leg in 2024; WPL uses rotating venues)
allTeams.owner: JSW GMR Cricket Pvt Ltd (JSW Group and GMR Group, 50% each)
allTeams.logoHistory: 2023–present: Uses the same blue shield with three tiger heads and Parliament-style dome as the IPL Delhi Capitals; no separate WPL logo era.
allTeams.notes: The WPL's 'nearly team': the only side to reach all four WPL finals (2023–2026) and lose every one. Meg Lanning captained in 2023–2025 before moving to UP Warriorz; Jemimah Rodrigues took over for 2026 and led DC to a fourth straight final.

allTeams.homeGround: BRSABV Ekana Cricket Stadium, Lucknow (hosted UPW's home leg in 2025; WPL uses rotating venues)
allTeams.owner: Capri Global Holdings Pvt Ltd (Capri Global Capital)
allTeams.nameHistory: UP Warriorz (2023–present) — name unchanged ('Warriorz' stylisation used since launch)
allTeams.logoHistory: 2023–present (single era): A shield emblem combining four elements — a Sarus crane in motion (the state bird of Uttar Pradesh), a sword, wings spread like a rising sun, and a shield — in yellow and purple; the identity pays tribute to Rani Lakshmi Bai of Jhansi.
allTeams.notes: Lucknow's WPL team, bought by Capri Global for ₹757 crore. Alyssa Healy captained in 2023–2025 (best finish: the 2023 Eliminator); a 2026 reset brought in Meg Lanning as captain and Abhishek Nayar as head coach. The team wears a special 'Rani Pink' jersey each year to promote girls' education.

allTeams.homeGround: Ahmedabad-based; BCA Stadium (Kotambi), Vadodara hosted Gujarat's home leg in 2025–2026 (WPL uses rotating venues)
allTeams.owner: Adani Sportsline Pvt Ltd (Adani Group)
allTeams.logoHistory: 2023–present (single era): A roaring Asiatic lioness in orange tones — the Asiatic lion is found only in Gujarat's Gir forest, and the lioness was chosen because lionesses hunt together in prides, symbolising teamwork. Logo unveiled on 12 February 2023.
allTeams.notes: The most expensive WPL franchise — Adani Sportsline paid ₹1,289 crore for it. Bottom of the table in 2023–2024, the Giants reached the playoffs for the first time in 2025 and made the Eliminator again in 2026 under captain Ashleigh Gardner.

coaches.name: Venkatesh Prasad
coaches.background: Former India fast bowler; was India's bowling coach (2007-2009) around the same period
coaches.achievements: Head coach for RCB's inaugural 2008 season (team finished 7th); moved to an assistant/bowling role when Ray Jennings took over for 2009
coaches.afterRcb: Later chaired the BCCI junior selection committee and served as Kings XI Punjab bowling coach (2018)

coaches.name: Martin Crowe
coaches.background: Former New Zealand captain and one of the game's leading batting thinkers
coaches.achievements: Held the top cricket role (chief cricketing officer) in RCB's first season, overseeing cricket operations and selection; resigned after the 2008 season
coaches.afterRcb: Remained a respected broadcaster and writer until his death in 2016

coaches.name: Ray Jennings
coaches.background: Former South Africa wicketkeeper and former South Africa national team coach, known as a strict disciplinarian
coaches.achievements: Longest-serving early head coach; led RCB to the 2009 IPL final, 2010 semi-finals, 2011 IPL final and the 2016-era core's foundation years; also coached RCB at the CLT20 in 2009, 2010 (semi-final) and 2011 (final); replaced after the 2013 season
coaches.afterRcb: Returned to coaching in South Africa; later worked with South African age-group/development sides (post-RCB roles thinly documented in sources checked)

coaches.name: Venkatesh Prasad
coaches.background: Former India fast bowler and India bowling coach
coaches.achievements: Stayed on as Jennings' assistant and bowling coach after handing over the head coach role in 2009; part of the staff for the 2009 and 2011 final runs and the CLT20 campaigns
coaches.afterRcb: See head coach row: BCCI junior selection committee chairman; KXIP bowling coach (2018)

coaches.name: Anil Kumble
coaches.background: India's greatest match-winning spinner; retired as RCB captain/player in January 2011
coaches.achievements: Appointed chief mentor straight after retiring as a player; mentored the side to the 2011 IPL final and the 2011 CLT20 final; left in January 2013
coaches.afterRcb: Became Mumbai Indians chief mentor (2013-2015, two titles); then India head coach (2016-2017) and Punjab Kings head coach/director (2020-2022)

coaches.name: Daniel Vettori
coaches.background: Former New Zealand captain and left-arm spinner; had played for RCB (2011-2013) before retiring
coaches.achievements: Appointed head coach in January 2014 after retiring as a player; led RCB to the 2016 IPL final (the 973-run Kohli season) and the 2015 playoffs; sacked in August 2018 after poor 2017-2018 seasons
coaches.afterRcb: Became Australia's assistant/spin bowling coach (2022 onwards) and Sunrisers Hyderabad head coach (from IPL 2024)

coaches.name: Allan Donald
coaches.background: Legendary South Africa fast bowler ('White Lightning'); former South Africa bowling coach
coaches.achievements: Appointed alongside Vettori in January 2014 as bowling coach; worked with RCB's pace attack through the 2016 final season (end year of tenure reported as 2016; see research notes)
coaches.afterRcb: Later served as Bangladesh fast bowling coach (2022-2023) among other consultancy roles

coaches.name: Trent Woodhill
coaches.background: Australian coach known for analytics and innovative methods; had worked with Melbourne Stars and New South Wales
coaches.achievements: Appointed batting and fielding coach in January 2014; in 2018 his role was broadened to batting talent development & analytics, fielding coach and head of scouting; removed in the August 2018 staff overhaul
coaches.afterRcb: Continued in Australian domestic/franchise coaching and talent-development roles

coaches.name: Bharat Arun
coaches.background: Former India seamer; coach of India's 2012 U-19 World Cup-winning team; India's bowling coach from 2014
coaches.achievements: Brought in as assistant coach for IPL 2015 only, alongside Vettori, Donald and Woodhill, while also serving as India's bowling coach; RCB reached the playoffs (qualifier 2) in 2015
coaches.afterRcb: Continued as India's bowling coach until 2021; later became Kolkata Knight Riders bowling coach (2022-2024)

coaches.name: Andrew McDonald
coaches.role: Bowling Coach / Bowling Talent Development and Analytics
coaches.background: Former Australia all-rounder; had coached Leicestershire and Victoria
coaches.achievements: Joined RCB in 2017 and served as bowling coach; for 2018 his brief shifted to bowling talent development and analytics when Ashish Nehra became bowling coach; removed in August 2018 overhaul (exact season split between the two roles is reported inconsistently - see research notes)
coaches.afterRcb: Became Australia assistant coach (2019) and then Australia head coach (2022 onwards), winning the 2023 ODI World Cup

coaches.name: Gary Kirsten
coaches.background: India's 2011 World Cup-winning head coach; former South Africa coach and Delhi Daredevils head coach
coaches.achievements: Joined in January 2018 as batting coach and mentor under head coach Daniel Vettori; elevated to the top job for 2019 after Vettori's sacking
coaches.afterRcb: See head coach row below

coaches.name: Gary Kirsten
coaches.background: As above; one of the most respected coaches in world cricket
coaches.achievements: Took over as head coach ('coach and mentor') for IPL 2019 under a split leadership model with bowling coach Ashish Nehra; RCB finished last (8th) and Kirsten was released in August 2019
coaches.afterRcb: Became Gujarat Titans batting coach and mentor (2022-2023, title in 2022) and Pakistan white-ball head coach (2024, resigned the same year)

coaches.name: Ashish Nehra
coaches.background: Former India left-arm fast bowler; retired from playing in November 2017 with no previous formal coaching experience
coaches.achievements: Joined in January 2018 as bowling coach and mentor under Vettori; retained when the rest of the 2018 staff was sacked and continued under Kirsten in 2019; released in August 2019
coaches.afterRcb: Became Gujarat Titans head coach from their debut season (2022), winning the IPL 2022 title and building one of the league's most consistent sides

coaches.name: Mike Hesson
coaches.background: Former New Zealand head coach (2012-2018, 2015 World Cup final); coached Kings XI Punjab in IPL 2019
coaches.achievements: Appointed in August 2019 as RCB's first Director of Cricket Operations under a single-coach model, overseeing strategy, scouting and auctions; built the squads that reached the playoffs in 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2024-cycle; contract not renewed in 2023
coaches.afterRcb: Appointed Pakistan men's white-ball head coach in 2025

coaches.name: Simon Katich
coaches.background: Former Australia opener; had been Kolkata Knight Riders assistant coach (2015-2019)
coaches.achievements: Appointed head coach in August 2019; led RCB to the playoffs in 2020 (their first since 2016) and to third place in the 2021 league stage; stepped down in August 2021 for personal reasons before the UAE leg of IPL 2021
coaches.afterRcb: Coached Manchester Originals in The Hundred (2021-2023)

coaches.name: Mike Hesson
coaches.background: As above - already RCB's Director of Cricket Operations
coaches.achievements: Stepped in as interim head coach for the UAE leg of IPL 2021 after Simon Katich stepped down, doubling up with his Director of Cricket role; RCB reached the Eliminator
coaches.afterRcb: Continued as Director of Cricket Operations (see main row)

coaches.name: Sanjay Bangar
coaches.background: Former India all-rounder; India's batting coach (2014-2019); previously Kochi Tuskers batting coach and Kings XI Punjab head coach (2014 final)
coaches.achievements: Joined as batting consultant in February 2021 for IPL 2021
coaches.afterRcb: Elevated to head coach for 2022 (see next row)

coaches.name: Adam Griffith
coaches.background: Former Tasmania fast bowler; Tasmania head coach and former Australia stand-in bowling coach; worked under Justin Langer at Western Australia/Perth Scorchers
coaches.achievements: Appointed in September 2019 as bowling coach, replacing Ashish Nehra; served five seasons (2020-2024) as pace-bowling lead under Katich, Bangar and Flower; replaced by Omkar Salvi after IPL 2024
coaches.afterRcb: Appointed Cricket Australia's National Pace Bowling Coach (2025)

coaches.name: Sridharan Sriram
coaches.background: Former India ODI all-rounder; long-time Australia spin consultant and assistant coach (Ashes and T20 World Cup wins); previously with Delhi and Punjab IPL franchises
coaches.achievements: Appointed in September 2019; batting and spin-bowling coach for IPL 2020, 2021 and 2022 under Katich and Bangar; left after IPL 2022
coaches.afterRcb: Became Bangladesh T20 technical consultant/head coach for the 2022 Asia Cup and T20 World Cup; Lucknow Super Giants assistant coach (2024); Chennai Super Kings assistant bowling coach (2025)

coaches.name: Sanjay Bangar
coaches.background: As above
coaches.achievements: Elevated from batting consultant to head coach in November 2021 for a two-year term; led RCB to the playoffs (Qualifier 2) in 2022 and sixth place in 2023; contract not renewed after 2023
coaches.afterRcb: Joined Punjab Kings as Head of Cricket Development ahead of IPL 2024 and continued media/commentary work

coaches.name: Malolan Rangarajan
coaches.background: Former Tamil Nadu offspinner; worked in Tamil Nadu cricket analysis and talent identification
coaches.achievements: Named Head of Scouting in RCB's 2020 staff list and became the franchise's lead scout/analyst across the Hesson and Bobat eras; also listed as fielding coach in the 2022 staff; remains RCB's lead scout and player-identification lead
coaches.afterRcb: Still with RCB (also WPL head coach from 2026 - see WPL rows)

coaches.name: Malolan Rangarajan
coaches.background: As above
coaches.achievements: Moved onto the men's coaching staff under Andy Flower: listed as assistant coach/fielding coach in 2024 and as spin bowling coach in 2025 and 2026 (cricket.one and ipl.com staff lists), part of the staff for the 2025 and 2026 title wins
coaches.afterRcb: Still with RCB

coaches.name: Shanker Basu
coaches.background: One of India's best-known fitness trainers; was RCB's trainer before becoming India's strength and conditioning coach (2015-2019, including the 2019 World Cup)
coaches.achievements: Returned to RCB in September 2019 for IPL 2020 and has remained head strength and conditioning coach through the Katich, Bangar and Flower eras, including the 2025 and 2026 titles; exact start year of his first RCB stint is not confirmed in sources checked
coaches.afterRcb: Still with RCB (active in IPL 2026)

coaches.name: Evan Speechly
coaches.tenure: Until 2025 (start year not verified; in role by the mid-2010s)
coaches.background: Physiotherapist with experience in South African cricket
coaches.achievements: Long-serving head of RCB's medical/physio setup, listed as team physio from the Vettori era through to IPL 2025 (ipl.com records him as serving until 2025)
coaches.afterRcb: Not listed in RCB's IPL 2026 staff

coaches.name: Soumyadeep Pyne
coaches.background: Former Indian Army officer (Major)
coaches.achievements: Listed as RCB team manager in the official IPL 2020 support staff announcement
coaches.afterRcb: Became Head of Operations for the RCB women's team in WPL 2023 (see WPL row)

coaches.name: Andy Flower
coaches.background: Former Zimbabwe captain and wicketkeeper; England head coach (2009-2014) who won the 2010 T20 World Cup and three Ashes series; title-winning franchise coach with Multan Sultans (PSL) and Trent Rockets (The Hundred); Lucknow Super Giants head coach (2022-2023)
coaches.achievements: Appointed in August 2023, replacing Sanjay Bangar; reunited with captain Faf du Plessis; led RCB to the playoffs in 2024 and then to the franchise's first IPL title in 2025 and back-to-back titles in 2026 (as recorded in this database)
coaches.afterRcb: Still RCB head coach through IPL 2026; also appointed London Spirit head coach in The Hundred from 2026

coaches.name: Mo Bobat
coaches.background: ECB performance director (2019-2024) who helped build England's 2019 ODI and 2022 T20 World Cup-winning pathways; at the ECB from 2011; had previously consulted for RCB
coaches.achievements: Appointed in September 2023 to replace Mike Hesson, overseeing recruitment and performance across the franchise; architect, with Andy Flower, of the squads that won IPL 2025 and 2026 and WPL 2026
coaches.afterRcb: Still with RCB

coaches.name: Dinesh Karthik
coaches.background: Former India wicketkeeper-batter; played for RCB in 2015 and 2022-2024, finishing his playing career at the franchise in 2024
coaches.achievements: Appointed in 2024 (after retiring as a player) as batting coach and mentor from IPL 2025; part of the coaching group for the 2025 and 2026 title wins; had previously worked with Omkar Salvi at KKR
coaches.afterRcb: Still with RCB (through IPL 2026)

coaches.name: Omkar Salvi
coaches.background: Mumbai head coach who won the Ranji Trophy and Irani Cup in 2023-24; previously Kolkata Knight Riders assistant bowling coach (part of KKR's IPL 2024 title staff); brother of former India pacer Aavishkar Salvi
coaches.achievements: Appointed on 18 November 2024, replacing Adam Griffith; joined after finishing Mumbai's domestic season in March 2025; bowling coach for the 2025 and 2026 title wins
coaches.afterRcb: Still with RCB (through IPL 2026)

coaches.name: Richard Halsall
coaches.background: Former England assistant coach and lead fielding coach under Andy Flower; Bangladesh assistant head coach/fielding coach; Sussex academy director; Multan Sultans fielding coach under Flower
coaches.achievements: Listed as RCB assistant coach in the 2025 staff (cricket.one) and as assistant coach/fielding support for IPL 2026 (ipl.com); profiled as RCB's fielding coach, a long-time Andy Flower ally
coaches.afterRcb: Still with RCB (listed for IPL 2026)

coaches.name: Freddie Wilde
coaches.background: Cricket data analyst and author associated with CricViz; co-author of 'Cricket 2.0'
coaches.achievements: Listed as RCB's performance analyst in the 2025 staff list (cricket.one) and team analyst for IPL 2026 (ipl.com), part of Mo Bobat's data-led setup
coaches.afterRcb: Still with RCB (listed for IPL 2026)

coaches.name: James Pipe
coaches.background: English physiotherapist
coaches.achievements: Listed as assistant physiotherapist in RCB's 2025 staff and as physiotherapist for IPL 2026, working under/alongside long-serving head physio Evan Speechly
coaches.afterRcb: Still with RCB (listed for IPL 2026)

coaches.name: Navnita Gautam
coaches.background: Sports therapist who also worked with the RCB women's team from its first season
coaches.achievements: Listed as sports massage therapist in RCB's 2022 staff and as athletic therapist in 2025-2026 staff lists; also head physio of the WPL side (see WPL row)
coaches.afterRcb: Still with RCB

coaches.name: Ramesh Mane
coaches.tenure: Listed from the mid-2010s to 2026 (exact start unverified)
coaches.background: Long-serving member of RCB's medical support unit
coaches.achievements: Appears as masseur in RCB staff lists from the Vettori era (alchetron/Wikipedia snapshot) through the IPL 2025 and 2026 lists - one of the franchise's longest-serving support staff
coaches.afterRcb: Still with RCB (listed for IPL 2026)

coaches.name: Dr. Shikha Dhaundiyal
coaches.background: Team doctor
coaches.achievements: Listed as RCB team doctor in the IPL 2026 staff list (ipl.com)
coaches.afterRcb: Still with RCB (listed for IPL 2026)

coaches.name: Mike Hesson
coaches.background: As above - RCB's franchise Director of Cricket Operations
coaches.achievements: Oversaw the women's team build for the inaugural WPL: announced the 2023 coaching staff and the auction strategy that bought Smriti Mandhana; RCB finished 4th in WPL 2023

franchise.details: At the BCCI's January 2008 franchise auction, Vijay Mallya's UB Group / United Spirits bought the Bengaluru franchise for US$111.6 million — the second-most expensive of the original eight (behind only Mumbai Indians). The team is named after United Spirits' Royal Challenge whisky brand; Mallya later said his 'sole purpose behind buying RCB was to promote my whisky brand.' Operating company: Royal Challengers Sports Pvt. Ltd. (RCSPL).

Diageo acquired control of United Spirits (majority by 2014), making RCB a Diageo-group asset. Mallya exited in 2016 amid his debt and legal troubles and has had no role since. Under USL the franchise professionalised — lifestyle verticals, the WPL team (2023), the Innovation Lab — and won back-to-back IPL titles in 2025–2026.

Vijay Mallya (founder-owner figure, 2008–2016) → chairmen including Amrit Thomas (mid-2010s), Anand Kripalu (early 2020s) and Prathmesh Mishra (mid-2020s). Rajesh V Menon — VP & Head from ~2020, referred to as CEO by 2025–26 — is the franchise's most visible executive of the decade.

November 2025: United Spirits announced a strategic review of RCB as a non-core asset. 24 March 2026: USL's board approved selling 100% of RCSPL — both the IPL and WPL teams — to a consortium of the Aditya Birla Group (lead), The Times Group, Bolt Ventures (David Blitzer) and Blackstone, for ₹16,660 crore (~US$1.78 billion), the biggest franchise sale in IPL history. The Competition Commission of India approved it on 30 June 2026; as of October 2026 no formal closing announcement had been reported, so ownership is best described as 'sold, pending formal completion', with Aryaman Vikram Birla named chairman and Satyan Gajwani (Times Group) vice-chairman. Value arc: $111.6m (2008) → ~$1.78bn (2026).

US$227 million (2024) → US$269 million (2025 — #1 in the IPL for the first time, after the maiden title) → US$312 million (2026 — still #1, and reported as the first cricket team anywhere to cross a $300 million brand value). Other firms' tables differ materially — always show the firm and year with any figure.

RCB's official name for its fans — the fans as the team's 12th player. The franchise addresses fans by this name across ticketing, social media and events, and built the Unbox festival around it. Related: the Bold Army (2016), an official cheer squad of superfans.

Kannada for 'This year, the cup is ours' — the defining slogan of the 17 title-less seasons, chanted at the Chinnaswamy and carried by the diaspora worldwide (fans were filmed chanting it at an India Women ODI in Brisbane in Dec 2024). After the WPL 2024 title fans flipped it to 'Ee Sala Cup Namdu' ('this year the cup IS ours'); the men's 2025 title retired the joke for good.

A sea of red and a reputation — repeated by visiting players and commentators — as one of the loudest, most atmospheric crowds in the IPL. RCB home fixtures routinely sell out within minutes of tickets opening (a formal consecutive-sellout streak is unverified).

Among the IPL's most-followed teams and widely reported as its most-engaged: ~45 million followers in total (Aug 2025 snapshot), with Instagram ~21.5–22 million — the most-followed IPL team account on Instagram. Multiple 2025 reports credit RCB with the IPL's highest fan engagement (~2 billion engagements in 2025, per aggregator reports).

Since ~2015, comedian Danish Sait as 'Mr. Nags' — a stereotypical Bengalurean superfan — has hosted RCB Insider's deliberately awkward player interviews and behind-the-scenes content; widely credited with pioneering IPL dressing-room content, he is the franchise's de-facto on-screen face. Long-running properties: Bold Diaries, 12th Man TV, the RCB app. A fan-first touch: a dog enclosure at the stadium for pet parents (a first in the IPL, per RCB).

Once a season since 2011, RCB swaps the red home kit for a green jersey to promote environmental awareness. First green match: 8 May 2011 vs Kochi Tuskers Kerala (won by 9 wickets). The jerseys are made from recycled material; the captain traditionally presents a sapling to the opposing captain at the toss.

14 May 2016 vs Gujarat Lions: Kohli (109) and AB de Villiers (129*) both scored hundreds in RCB's 248/3, a 144-run win. In 2021 RCB wore blue instead, honouring COVID-19 frontline workers. Green-game record before the 2026 edition: 15 played, 5 won, 9 lost, 1 no-result.

RCB states it is the world's only carbon-neutral T20 franchise and is working toward carbon-positive status, alongside stadium waste/recycling measures, fan-travel carbon surveys and (with Goodera) Bengaluru lake rejuvenation and a 'green schools' programme. This is a franchise claim — no independent certification was found in public sources.

The pre-season fan festival. 2022 (Church Street): first edition; Faf du Plessis announced as captain. 2023 (Chinnaswamy): moved into the stadium; the RCB Hall of Fame launched. 2024: the Bengaluru name change and new crest unveiled, with a headline performance by Alan Walker. It has run annually since.
Inducted at Unbox 2023. RCB 2011–17: 3,420 runs, five hundreds, the 175*. His jersey number 333 was retired.

franchise.item: Hall of Fame — AB de Villiers (2023)
franchise.details: Inducted at Unbox 2023. RCB 2011–21: 4,522 runs in 157 matches. His jersey number 17 was retired.

franchise.item: Hall of Fame — R Vinay Kumar (2024)
franchise.details: Inducted at Unbox 2024. RCB's third-highest wicket-taker (80 wickets); led RCB's bowling in 2012 and 2013. No further inductions were reported through October 2026.

'Jeetenge Hum Shaan Se' (earliest theme) → 'Game for More' (2009, hugely popular) → 'Play Bold' (2016, composed by Salim Merchant, released in six languages) — 'Play Bold' doubles as the franchise philosophy. Alan Walker produced a special RCB track for Unbox 2024. Other stock phrases: 'We Are Challengers', 'Namma RCB'.

The crest's rampant lion is the franchise symbol and appears as a costumed mascot at matches (one blog names it 'Chinnaswamy' — unverified in official sources). In practice, Mr. Nags is the public face of the franchise off the field.

Launched 26 March 2023: sports ed-tech, performance R&D, health-tech startup accelerators and an AI-backed coaching/talent-ID platform. Its first international tie-up, with Leaders in Sport, produced the Leaders Meet India conclave in Bengaluru (29–30 Nov 2023) — speakers included Jay Shah, Brendon McCullum, Neeraj Chopra and Abhinav Bindra.

Launched December 2020 on St Mark's Road / Church Street, Bengaluru (under a kilometre from the stadium); a second outlet opened at Kempegowda International Airport Terminal 2 in February 2024. Match screenings, player portraits, RCB-themed menu.

PUMA x RCB athleisure range (from 2021); Hustle by RCB fitness app (~11,000 subscriptions in its first three months, per a 2024 interview); the RCB official app for ticketing, gaming and content — the stated ambition is 'India's sports super app.'

First IPL team with separate home and away kits (2016). Most valuable IPL franchise in 2025 and 2026 (Houlihan Lokey). Biggest franchise sale in IPL history (2026). Most-followed IPL team on Instagram. And the most expensive buy of the first WPL auction (below).

On 25 January 2023 the BCCI sold the five WPL teams; RCSPL won Bengaluru for ₹901 crore — the third-most expensive of the five. RCB had prepared for months, appointing former India cricketer Vanitha V. R. as scout well before the tender.

A front-loaded, star-led strategy: ₹9 crore of the ₹12 crore purse went on the first five players — Smriti Mandhana ₹3.40 cr (the auction's top price and immediately captain), Richa Ghosh ₹1.90 cr, Ellyse Perry ₹1.70 cr, Renuka Singh ₹1.50 cr, and the steal of the auction, Sophie Devine for ₹50 lakh. Depth picks added three more international captains (Knight, van Niekerk, Schutt) and ₹10-lakh bargains Shreyanka Patil and Asha Sobhana — both title-winners in 2024.

Two days after the women won WPL 2024 in Delhi, they were the centrepiece of Unbox 2024 at the Chinnaswamy: the full men's squad formed a guard of honour as Mandhana led the champions in with the trophy, and during the victory lap she video-called the absent Ellyse Perry so she could share the moment — the defining image of RCB as one club.

franchise.item: The first trophy was the women's
franchise.details: RCB Women's 2024 WPL title was the franchise's first-ever trophy — a year before the men's. With the women's 2026 title and the men's 2025–26 double, RCB became the first franchise to hold IPL and WPL crowns in the same period. Both teams were sold together in the 2026 ownership sale.

rcbCares.details: 3 June 2025, Ahmedabad: RCB beat Punjab Kings by 6 runs to win their first IPL title in 18 seasons. The team flew home to Bengaluru the next day.

RCB announced an open-top bus parade from Vidhana Soudha to the Chinnaswamy Stadium. Bengaluru Police DENIED permission for the parade (traffic/CBD concerns). A state felicitation at the Vidhana Soudha and a stadium ceremony went ahead instead. The D'Cunha commission later found RCB had informed police on 3 June but had not obtained the mandatory permission (applications are required 7+ days ahead) and had shared no crowd estimate or security plan.

An estimated 2–3 lakh (200,000–300,000) people gathered in the streets around a stadium whose capacity is about 35,000. A 3:14 pm RCB social post about free passes added confusion, and rumours of free tickets spread at the gates.

Between about 3:30 and 5:30 pm, crowd crushes occurred at gates 1, 2/2A, 6, 7, 15, 17, 18 and 20/21 as fans forced barricades and gates were shut and opened under pressure. A temporary slab over a drain near the stadium also gave way. Deaths were recorded at hospitals from 3:45 pm to 5:15 pm.

11 fans died and 56 were injured (the settled official figure). All eleven were under 40; the youngest was 13. Even as the crush unfolded, the Vidhana Soudha felicitation (4–5 pm) went ahead; the stadium ceremony was cut short once casualty reports emerged.

Names and details are taken from published news reports, primarily the Indian Express account built from hospital records placed before the Karnataka High Court. Early lists also carried a name, 'Doresha (32)', which appears in no later, fuller account and is treated as an early reporting error. Ages marked with notes differ between early lists and hospital records — the discrepancies are shown rather than hidden.

RCB announced ₹10 lakh to the family of each fan who died, pledged to cover the injured fans' medical expenses, and created a fund for injured fans — the first use of the name 'RCB Cares'. Virat Kohli: 'At a loss for words. Absolutely gutted.'

After nearly three months of social-media silence ('The silence was not absence, but grief'), RCB formally launched RCB Cares and announced ₹25 lakh to each of the eleven families — 'not just as financial aid, but as a promise of compassion, unity, and ongoing care.'

₹10 lakh compensation per bereaved family and free treatment for all injured; magisterial inquiry, a CID/SIT probe, and a one-man judicial commission were ordered; crowd-management SOPs for large gatherings followed.

Cubbon Park Police Station, Crime No. 123/2025 — accused: (1) RCB (Royal Challengers Sports Pvt. Ltd.), (2) DNA Entertainment Networks, (3) the KSCA Administrative Committee, under BNS sections including 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder).

Arrested 6 June 2025: Nikhil Sosale (RCB head of marketing & revenue) and DNA Entertainment officials Sunil Mathew, Kiran and Sumanth (later interim bail). KSCA secretary A. Shankar and treasurer E. S. Jairam resigned citing moral responsibility. Five police officers including Commissioner B. Dayananda were suspended — the Central Administrative Tribunal quashed Dayananda's suspension on 1 July 2025, holding RCB prima facie responsible.

Retired Justice John Michael D'Cunha's report (11 July 2025) held RCB, KSCA, DNA Entertainment and the police responsible through negligence: no official permission, free-entry announcements made without consulting police, gates not opened on time, no ambulances on site. The state cabinet accepted the report on 24 July 2025 and ordered legal action. The stadium was declared unsuitable for large events pending 17 corrective measures — Bengaluru lost its 2025 Women's World Cup matches as a result.

The CID prepared a chargesheet of about 2,200 pages (Nov 2025), but the Karnataka High Court has directed that it not be filed without the court's leave; quash petitions by RCB, DNA and Sosale and the High Court's suo motu crowd-safety case remain pending. No trial outcome has been reported.

12 February 2026: conditional cabinet clearance after safety works — widened gates, internal holding areas, marked emergency access, ramps, fully digital ticketing, and 300–350 AI-enabled CCTV cameras proposed and funded by RCB (~₹4.5 crore). RCB played five home games at Chinnaswamy and two in Raipur in IPL 2026.

Announced 27 March 2026 by RCB CEO Rajesh Menon: eleven seats in the P1 stand at Chinnaswamy will remain permanently unoccupied at all matches — 'a quiet tribute to their memory.' Players wear No. 11 practice/warm-up jerseys through the season and black armbands, and a memorial plaque stands near the stadium's inner entrance.

Before RCB vs Sunrisers Hyderabad — the first match at Chinnaswamy since the tragedy — players, officials and fans observed a minute's silence; both teams wore black armbands; RCB warmed up in No. 11 jerseys; KSCA unveiled the memorial plaque.

31 May 2026: RCB beat Gujarat Titans to win back-to-back titles. There was deliberately NO victory parade and no public celebration in Bengaluru (police advisory; RCB asked fans to celebrate at home). Captain Rajat Patidar dedicated the trophy to the eleven: 'We dedicate this trophy to our fans — actually not fans, family members — who passed away in the tragedy last year.'

No separate large public event was reported for the first anniversary (4 June 2026); remembrance centred on the March tributes and the trophy dedication. Discussions on further support for the families were reported as ongoing under RCB Cares. The stadium hosted its first international since the tragedy — India v West Indies T20I — on 17 October 2026.

RCB's long-term commitment platform, born of the tragedy: first announced as a fund for injured fans on 5 June 2025, formally launched 30 August 2025, with its framework published on 1 September 2025 — 'a long-term commitment to support, empower and elevate our 12th Man Army.'
Fast, transparent and human support to impacted fans and families.
Work with stadium authorities, sporting bodies and league partners to design better crowd-management protocols.
Social development programmes in rural Karnataka, beginning with the Siddi community (reported as already begun by Sept 2025).
Fund independent research, create a fan-safety audit framework, and train on-ground partners annually on crowd management and emergency response.

'Elevate fan memory into something permanent' — a dedicated space in Bengaluru honouring the names, stories and spirit of RCB's fans. The Chinnaswamy memorial plaque and the eleven empty seats are its visible fulfilment.
Create in-stadia jobs, nurture local talent, and support the next generation of sports professionals.

rcbCares.item: Not the same as Go Green
rcbCares.details: RCB's environmental programme (the Green Game, since 2011) is older and separate from RCB Cares — the two should not be conflated.
